title: The Lion, the Mouse, and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Lion was lying asleep at the mouth of his den when a Mouse ran over his back and tickled him so that he woke up with a start and began looking about everywhere to see what it was that had disturbed him. A Fox, who was looking on, thought he would have a joke at the expense of the Lion; so he said, "Well, this is the first time I've seen a Lion afraid of a Mouse." "Afraid of a Mouse?" said the Lion testily: "not I! It's his bad manners I can't stand."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Lion lying when the Mouse ran over him?
options: At the mouth of his den

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Mouse do to the Lion?
options: Ran over his back and tickled him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Lion do after waking with a start?
options: Began looking about everywhere to see what had disturbed him
Chased the Mouse into the den

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Fox think he would do at the Lion's expense?
According to the passage, what does the Fox say he has never seen before?
options: A Lion afraid of a Mouse
A Lion living so close to a den

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Lion say he cannot stand about the Mouse?
Based on the passage, why does the Lion insist it was not fear that made him wake with a start?
options: He wants to protect his pride and reject the Fox's suggestion that a mouse could frighten him
He genuinely believes the Mouse is a serious threat to him
He is too tired to argue with the Fox properly
He agrees with the Fox but wants to blame someone else

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Someone caught off guard may deny fear by claiming to be offended instead
Foxes are always more clever than lions in every situation
Mice are more dangerous to lions than most animals realize
Lions should never sleep near the entrance of their dens

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who was watching and looking on while the Lion woke up?
According to the passage, how does the passage describe the way the Lion answered the Fox?
According to the passage, what question does the Lion repeat back to the Fox?
Based on the passage, why does the Fox choose this particular moment to tease the Lion?
options: He had just witnessed the Lion visibly startled by something as small as a mouse
He had overheard the Lion complaining about mice earlier that day
He wanted to distract the Lion so the Mouse could escape
He was jealous that the Mouse had gotten so close to the Lion

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "testily" mean in "said the Lion testily"?
options: In a calm and patient manner
In a whisper meant only for the Fox

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox teases a startled Lion for seeming afraid of a Mouse, and the Lion insists he was only annoyed, not frightened
A Lion chases a Fox away after being teased by a Mouse
A Mouse and a Fox work together to frighten a sleeping Lion
A Lion thanks the Mouse for waking him before danger arrived
